papers.title: ZGCM-1: A Fully Open and Extremely Efficient Foundation Model for Math and Agentic Search
papers.innovation: ZGCM-1 is a fully open, 7B dense foundation model trained from scratch with extreme data, system, and algorithmic efficiency. It demonstrates that compact models can overcome parametric capacity limits by coupling deliberation with external tools, making it highly valuable for resource-constrained deployments.
papers.benchmarks: While specific benchmarks are not detailed in the abstract, the emphasis on 'extreme efficiency' implies strong performance metrics related to training cost, inference latency, throughput, and resource footprint, alongside competitive accuracy on math and agentic search tasks.
papers.use_case: Deploying highly efficient, open-source foundation models for specialized tasks such as mathematical reasoning and agentic search, particularly in environments with limited computational resources or requiring low latency and cost-effectiveness.

papers.title: Root-Cause Attribution Is a Search Problem: Continual Search for Long-Horizon Agent Failures
papers.innovation: This paper frames root-cause attribution for long-horizon AI agent failures as a continual search problem. This innovative approach provides a systematic and scalable method to diagnose issues from massive execution logs, transforming outcome-level signals into actionable interventions which is critical for system reliability.
papers.benchmarks: Implied benchmarks would include the efficiency and accuracy of identifying root causes of failures in complex, long-horizon agent execution logs, likely comparing against existing diagnostic methods or manual analysis.
papers.use_case: Debugging, monitoring, and maintaining robust AI agent systems, especially those operating in long-horizon or complex environments, by automating and streamlining the identification of underlying causes for operational failures from extensive log data.

papers.title: OrchSLM: Probing the Dynamics of Small Language Model Orchestration
papers.innovation: This work explores the orchestration of Small Language Models (SLMs) to address fundamental challenges associated with deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) in agentic pipelines, such as high latency, privacy concerns, connectivity issues, and substantial computational costs. It provides key insights into the practical dynamics and benefits of SLM cooperation.
papers.benchmarks: Expected benchmarks would involve comparative analysis of orchestrated SLM systems versus single LLM deployments across metrics like latency, throughput, computational resource consumption, cost-effectiveness, and privacy, within the context of agentic workflows.
papers.use_case: Designing and implementing efficient, cost-effective, and privacy-preserving AI agent pipelines by leveraging the collective intelligence of multiple small language models, making it particularly relevant for edge deployments or scenarios with strict resource or data privacy constraints.
